official.deadline_note: The non-EU/EEA application deadline is 15 January (EU/EEA: 1 March), and it also covers the application fee, the English language documentation and the waiver statement. Non-EU/EEA applicants with a qualifying degree from Denmark must also apply by 15 January to be considered for the waiver. Tuition fee payment deadline for newly admitted non-EU/EEA students is 1 May, waivers are announced in April, and final documents are due 15 July.
official.application_cycle: Autumn intake - application portal opens 1 December, non-EU/EEA deadline 15 January (next round: autumn 2027). Tuition fee waivers are not offered for the spring intake.
official.status_note: DTU publishes one autumn timeline for MSc applicants: the portal opens 1 December, the non-EU/EEA deadline is 15 January, and tuition fee waivers are announced in April for eligible non-EU/EEA applicants after admission. The next 15 January deadline following the 10 October 2026 verification date is 15 January 2027 for the autumn 2027 intake.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: a tuition fee waiver will cover the tuition fee for two years. The tuition fee for paying students is 7500 EUR per semester, i.e. a total of 30000 EUR for two years of MSc studies, and DTU notes that tuition fees are likely to be revised for the autumn 2026 intake.
official.funding_period: per two-year MSc (covers tuition for two years)

official.citizenship_residency: Awarded only to citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA. Non-EU/EEA applicants with a qualifying degree from Denmark must apply by 15 January to be considered. Separately, non-EU/EEA citizens holding certain Danish residence permits are exempt from tuition altogether.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the waiver exists specifically for international non-EU/EEA students; EU/EEA students pay no tuition in Denmark and are not part of this award.
official.research_requirement: The personal statement for the waiver must focus on academic achievements at the Bachelor's level, and research experience or publications are among the published selection criteria. No research proposal is required.

official.description: DTU has a very limited number of tuition fee waivers to award international new non-EU/EEA MSc students applying for the Autumn intake, allocated to students with excellent academic performance. A tuition fee waiver covers the tuition fee for two years, is decided in parallel with admissions, and is granted after the applicant accepts an offer of admission.
official.program_type: Merit-based tuition fee waiver for MSc students, awarded in parallel with admission
official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 per section; TOEFL iBT new scale 4.5 overall with 4.0 per section for tests taken on or after 21 January 2026 (old scale: 92 overall with 22 per section); Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 180. DTU must receive the documentation by the application deadline, no exemptions are granted, and a degree where English was the language of instruction is not accepted as proof.

applicant_utility.summary: Apply by 15 January and treat the waiver as a bonus on top of admission, not as funding for your stay: it waives tuition only, so you still need to cover roughly two years of living costs in Denmark yourself. The application only counts for the waiver if a separate personal statement focused on your bachelor-level academic achievements is uploaded with the same application, since DTU ignores late or missing ones. Book your IELTS or TOEFL early, because official scores must be in DTU's hands by the same 15 January cut-off and DTU grants no exemptions, not even for degrees taught in English. With only a very limited number of waivers in existence and outcomes landing in April, pair this application with a concrete budget plan before you accept the offer.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants to a two-year DTU MSc with a strong bachelor transcript from a well-ranked university who can self-fund living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the whole application in one go once the portal opens on 1 December - DTU lists uploading documents after submission among its common mistakes.

Write a waiver-specific statement on bachelor-level academic achievements (grades, research, publications) that is clearly labelled as the tuition fee waiver statement, kept separate from any programme motivation letter.
Sit IELTS Academic or TOEFL iBT by October or November so official reports are ready for the 15 January cut-off; DTU rejects 'My Best Scores' and does not accept an English-taught degree as proof.
Pay the 100 EUR application fee in the DTU Webshop using exactly the same full name and email as your DANS application, then keep and upload the receipt.
Fill every sheet of the mandatory qualification template with ECTS conversions and live course links and submit it as .xlsx, never converted to PDF.
Get transcripts and diploma signed and stamped (or carrying a verification code), officially translated into English, and merge all course descriptions with their official URLs into one PDF.
common_rejection_risks: No separate waiver statement attached to the application - DTU states the application will not be considered for the waiver at all.
Language documentation missing or late: there are no exemptions, and incomplete or unclear documentation disqualifies the whole admission application.
Application fee not registered by 15 January - DTU does not process the application until the payment is registered.
Qualification template submitted as a PDF, only partly filled, with missing ECTS conversions, an unfilled distribution segment or broken course links.
Uncertified transcript or diploma scans, or documents not officially translated into English.
Applying for the spring intake, for which DTU does not offer waivers at all.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, travel, health insurance and the 100 EUR application fee. The waiver covers tuition only and DTU publishes no stipend, so you must fund your stay in Denmark and meet Denmark's residence-permit funds requirements yourself.
document_audit: The waiver statement is its own upload - a motivation letter on academic achievements, grades and research experience - never folded into the CV or the programme letter.
The qualification template must stay in .xlsx: DTU lists converting it to PDF as a common mistake, and every sheet including the distribution segment must be completed.
Course descriptions must form one merged English PDF with each official course URL visible, and the same links must work inside the qualification template.

Transcripts and diplomas must be certified (signed and stamped, or with a verification code) with official English translations; DTU verifies documents with issuing institutions and punishes falsified ones with disqualification.

Two recommendation letters as separate PDFs are required only for Biomedical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Design and Innovation, Engineering Acoustics, Mechanical Engineering and Sustainable Energy Technologies - confirm whether your programme is on that list.
Upload proof of the 100 EUR application fee; the fee covers one intake and your 1st and 2nd priority programme, is non-refundable, and must be paid again for another intake.
alerts: 15 January is a quadruple deadline: application, application fee, English documentation and the waiver statement all have to be in place that day.
The waiver is only announced in April and is granted after you accept the admission offer, so it never removes the need for a parallel funding or budget plan.
Applicants without a waiver still face the 1 May autumn tuition deadline, with a first instalment of 7400 EUR because the 100 EUR application fee is offset.

DTU states tuition fees are likely to be revised for the autumn 2026 intake, so the 7500 EUR per semester / 30000 EUR two-year figure is the currently published level and should be re-checked before you rely on it.
The waiver is limited to new non-EU/EEA students for the autumn intake - continuing students and spring applicants are excluded.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the MSc application in DANS with all documents and the waiver statement by 15 January, pay the 100 EUR fee in the DTU Webshop with matching details, DTU processes the application only after the payment registers, admission and waiver assessment run in parallel, waivers are announced in April, and accepting the offer activates the two-year tuition waiver.
